newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Leader of new Jamaican political party shot.
newsitem.headline: Leader of new Jamaican political party shot.

text.p: The general secretary of Jamaica's newest political party has been shot and wounded in an attack that the party said on Tuesday was politically motivated to intimidate its members.

Brascoe Lee of the National Democratic Movement was shot by two assailants on Monday as he conversed with them through the window of his home in rural western Jamaican, police said. The two supposedly approached Lee to warn him about plans for an attempt on his life but shot him instead, hitting him in the arm, police said.

Lee, 56, is one of 11 leading members of the opposition Jamaica Labour Party who split with JLP leader Edward Seaga in early 1995 to form the NDM. General elections are not due until mid 1998 but are expected to be called later this year.

NDM president Bruce Golding, another of the 11 dissidents, said on Tuesday the shooting was "an unmistakable political assassination attempt." He said several NDM candidates had been targets of "intimidatory tactics" in the past six months.
Prime Minister P.J. Patterson expressed regret about the shooting, calling for an "urgent and thorough investigation."
But JLP general secretary Edmund Bartlett referred to an "alleged shooting" and said it required "a full and thorough investigation with full disclosure of the circumstances surrounding the event."
